text:
1. Install the AWS CLI on Windows
You need the execution file to run AWS commands.
• Download: Get the 64-bit Windows MSI Installer.
• Install: Run the .msi file. It’s a standard "Next, Next, Finish" wizard.
• Confirm: Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and type:
aws --version
If you see "aws is not recognized," close and restart your terminal to refresh the system
path.
2. Generate Your Keys (AWS Console)
If you don't have your keys yet, you must get them from the AWS Web Console:
1. Log in to your AWS Account and search for IAM.
2. Click Users on the left and select your username.
3. Go to the Security credentials tab.
4. Scroll to Access keys and click Create access key.
5. Select Command Line Interface (CLI), check the "I understand..." box, and click Next.
6. Crucial: Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.
Tip: Download the .csv file. This is the only time AWS will ever show you the
Secret Key.
3. Link the Keys to Windows
This is where you "log in" locally.
1. In your Windows PowerShell, type:
aws configure

2. The CLI will prompt you for four pieces of information. Paste them in order:
• AWS Access Key ID: AKIAXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX 
• AWS Secret Access Key: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY 
• Default region name: us-east-1 (or your preferred region)
• Default output format: json 
4. Where are these keys stored?
On Windows, your credentials are not stored in your environment variables by default. They
are saved in a hidden folder in your user profile:
• Path: C:\Users\YourUserName\.aws\ 
• Files: * credentials : Contains your Secret and Access keys.
◦ config : Contains your region and output settings.
